name: Eval Gap Research
stats: 1.00 vs 0.31 good vs bad separation · n = 8, early results
content: Eval Gap Research (In Progress): "How do you grade an AI when there's no right answer?". AI agents improve fast wherever there's a test to pass. Most real tasks have no test. This project asks whether an AI judge with a checklist can fill that gap, and measures when its confidence can be trusted. Key highlights: **The scores work:** good and bad output separate cleanly. **The confidence signal doesn't, yet:** subtly wrong answers still scored full marks, and the experiment shows why. Honest limitation/tradeoff: Eight examples on one model, so it's directional only. Next: rubrics from several different models. Verified metrics: 1.00 vs 0.31 good vs bad separation · n = 8, early results.
